sections.html:
Cecil County is the northeastern corner of Maryland, touching Pennsylvania and Delaware. Elkton is the county seat and the largest town. The 2020 census counted 103,725 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 107,131.

Elkton had 6,386 housing units in 2020, with 6.9% of them vacant. That is a thin supply of empty homes, so a tidy house priced sensibly is not up against piles of empty stock. About 72 of the county's 418 square miles are water, so owners near the bay and the Elk River should expect flood and drainage questions from buyers and lenders.

The county rate is $0.9724 per $100 of assessed value, down from $0.9824. The state adds $0.112, so a house outside any town pays $1.0844 per $100. Towns add their own rate on top, and the town rate is the main reason two houses in the same county can carry very different bills.

Elkton carries the highest combined rate among the towns. A buyer comparing an Elkton house with a same-priced house in the open county will see a noticeably bigger bill, and you should be ready for that conversation.

Residential full cash value in Cecil County rose 15.1% between January 1, 2023 and January 1, 2026. Statewide, the comparable group rose 13.2%. Notices were mailed December 30, 2025, and the increase is phased in evenly over three years, so the taxable value on a bill can trail the new market value for a while.

The county's assessable base is about $14.6 billion for fiscal 2026, with $15.4 billion projected for fiscal 2027.

Homestead credit

An owner who lives in the house applies once for the homestead credit, which holds yearly increases in taxable value to the local cap. The cap for unincorporated Cecil County is 4% for July 1, 2026. Counties and towns can change their caps until March 15, so check the current number with the assessment office. A buyer does not inherit your capped value, because the cap resets after a sale, which is worth mentioning when a buyer asks what the bill will be.

Bills are mailed in July. An annual bill can be paid without interest through September and becomes delinquent on October 1. Owners of a principal residence can instead pay half by September 30 and half by December 31. Semi-annual billing is also open to some commercial property.

Delinquent balances accrue 1% interest per month, and a 3% late fee is added on March 1.

  • Pay at the Finance Office, 200 Chesapeake Blvd., Suite 1100, Elkton, or online.
  • E-check and card payments carry a third-party convenience fee.
  • From May 1, taxes must be paid with cash, a cashier's or certified check, a money order or certain credit cards.
  • A returned check costs $35.
  • If a lender escrows your tax, the lender can see bills electronically. Forward your own copy anyway.

Rate questions go to tax@ccgov.org. The state assessment office answers at 410-996-2760.

sections.h2: How the Cecil County tax sale works
sections.html:
The county sells unpaid tax online each June through RealAuction. In 2025, pre-registration ran May 16 to 23, bidding opened May 31, and the sale closed in early June. Call the Finance Office for the current schedule, because the closing time can shift.

  1. Delinquency notices go out March 1.
  2. The sale is advertised in a local newspaper for four consecutive weeks.
  3. Bidders pre-register and pay a $100 non-refundable deposit.
  4. If a winning bid runs above 40% of the property's full cash value, the buyer pays a 20% premium on the excess. That premium comes back if the certificate is redeemed or foreclosed within two years.

You can redeem until a court forecloses the right of redemption. A buyer may start a foreclosure case six months and one day after the sale. The county does not handle foreclosure itself.

sections.h2: Credits and deferrals that matter when you sell
sections.html:
The county offers a Senior Tax Credit and a second credit for former service members, each worth 20% off the county tax. Thresholds include household income under $92,000 and a dwelling assessed at $375,000 or less, with a September 1 deadline. State credits, exemptions and a deferral program are also available.

The elderly and disabled deferral is the one that changes a closing. It defers only the county tax increase over the prior year, and the deferred amount becomes a recorded lien that is repaid when the owner sells or moves out.

  • Owners 65 or older with five years of residency may qualify, with household income of $60,000 or less.
  • A recorded lien shows up in the title search, so the title company adds it to the payoff.
  • Other exemptions include $15,000 off the assessment for blind owners and a full exemption for disabled service members with a 100% permanent service-connected disability.

Credit amounts and limits change, so confirm them with the Finance Office before you tell a buyer what the bill will look like. If you are still living in the house, ask whether any credit you hold ends at the sale, and whether the county will prorate the bill between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. Proration is normally handled by the title company, but the numbers it uses come from the Finance Office records, so an old address or a missing credit on file can throw the figures off.

Call the Finance Office first, then go down this list.

  1. Ask what is owed and whether the account has been sent to the June sale.
  2. Check for a deferral lien left from a past credit program.
  3. Find out whether a town bill also applies, for example in Elkton or North East.
  4. Order a payoff figure good through your closing date, since interest runs at 1% a month.

At closing, the title company pays the county and any town from your proceeds, and the settlement statement shows each line. If the house also needs repairs, a cash sale as-is puts the tax payoff on that statement and stops the monthly penalties without a round of fix-ups, inspections and repair credits.

Bring the latest bill, any deferral paperwork and your homestead approval to the first call. It saves a second trip. If a town bill and a county bill both apply, ask for two separate payoffs, because the town and the county are paid as different accounts and each has its own interest clock. Once both are paid, ask for written confirmation and keep it with your closing papers in case a lender or buyer asks later.

faqs.q: What is the Cecil County real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is $0.9724 per $100 of assessed value, with $0.112 more for the state. That makes $1.0844 per $100 outside a town.

faqs.q: Which Cecil County town has the highest property tax?
faqs.a: Elkton, at a combined $1.7200 per $100. Cecilton is lowest among the listed towns at $1.4109.

faqs.q: What interest and penalties apply to late Cecil County tax?
faqs.a: Delinquent balances accrue 1% interest per month, and a 3% late fee is added on March 1.

faqs.q: When is the Cecil County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held online each June. In 2025 bidding opened May 31 and the sale closed in early June.

faqs.q: Must a tax deferral be repaid when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. A deferred amount is recorded as a lien and has to be repaid when the owner sells or moves out.
